done_when: The guard allows rm -rf when every target, resolved, is inside the system temp folder (TMPDIR, /tmp or /private/tmp), and allows reading git config values (git config --get, or git config with a key and no value); everything it blocks today otherwise stays blocked.

findings.body: An inherited variable can turn one apparent temp target into multiple shell targets. With FOO='safe /etc', `rm -rf /tmp/$FOO` passes: expandvars produces the single string `/tmp/safe /etc`, which realpath considers inside `/tmp`. The shell splits the unquoted expansion into `/tmp/safe` and `/etc`, so the guard permits a removal it previously blocked. Check the shell's resulting targets or reject expansions whose value can split.

findings.body: The end-to-end blocked cases test an unset variable and variable reassignment, but none tests an inherited variable containing whitespace. Add a `forge hook deny` case with FOO='safe /etc' and `rm -rf /tmp/$FOO`; it must be refused. The current test passes while that command is allowed.
findings.title: Not done: Test inherited-variable splitting at the deny hook

findings.body: `rm -rf /tmp/clone=v2` has one literal target inside the temp folder, but the global `=` breaker makes `alone` false and the guard refuses it. An equals sign in an argument cannot assign a shell variable before `rm` runs. Restrict the assignment safeguard to command prefixes so this valid temp target is allowed.
findings.title: Allow equals signs in temp target names

findings.body: `rm -rf /tmp/parent/../clone` resolves to `/tmp/clone`, but the unconditional `..` check refuses it. The existing realpath and root containment check can determine whether such a target remains inside temp; retain the refusal when it resolves outside.
findings.title: Allow resolved temp paths with internal parent components

why: The destructive-command guard blocks rm -rf even inside the system temp folder where coordinators keep scratch clones, and blocks reading a git config value, so scratch clones pile up and coordinators work around the guard
